page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 945 GB disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable strength, achieving a top-tier rating in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average range. Memory performance shows a distinct tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. LLM inference text generation for small models is strong, while medium model performance remains average.

Due to its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers a cost-effective option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The inclusion of 945 GB of local storage provides high resource density for temporary data. It is well-suited for web serving, text processing, software compilation, and light machine learning inference tasks where single-core speed is prioritized over massive memory capacity.
